exposure: Adherence to pregnancy-specific primary immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) clinical guidelines
outcome: Adherence to ITP clinical guidelines (for severe, mild, and moderate thrombocytopenia)
Unnecessary treatment for moderate asymptomatic thrombocytopenia
cohort: The study included 85 pregnant persons diagnosed with primary immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) who received care at the University of Oklahoma Health system between 2011 and 2020.
finding: While management for severe thrombocytopenia was 100% adherent to guidelines, approximately 40% of pregnant individuals with ITP received unnecessary treatment for moderate asymptomatic thrombocytopenia, either during pregnancy or for epidural anesthesia.
mod_finding: A majority (68%) of participants delivered vaginally, and 38% received unnecessary treatment to increase platelet counts for epidural anesthesia despite guideline suggestions.
